rics.description: Brave-Butters-Kelley Indexes, Coincident Index
rics.meaning: Brave-Butters-Kelley Coincident Index — current economic activity. Real-time GDP-tracking proxy.
rics.how_to_use: Tracks GDP contemporaneously. Decelerations precede recession by 0-3 months. Use BBK Leading for forward read, BBK Coincident for current state.

rics.description: Brave-Butters-Kelley Indexes, Leading Index
rics.meaning: Brave-Butters-Kelley Leading Index — a forward-looking activity gauge constructed from a panel of macro indicators. Federal Reserve Bank of Chicago.
rics.how_to_use: Negative readings precede recessions with ~6-12mo lead. Less widely-tracked than the Conference Board LEI but methodologically rigorous. Pair with the BBK Coincident for full picture.

rics.description: Brave-Butters-Kelley Indexes, Monthly GDP Growth (Annualized), %
rics.meaning: BBK Monthly GDP Growth rate, annualized. Monthly nowcast of GDP — the BBK team's translation of activity data into a GDP-equivalent rate.
rics.how_to_use: Compare to Atlanta Fed's GDPNow and NY Fed's Nowcast for consensus on current-quarter GDP. Useful between BEA releases for tracking cycle.

rics.description: Brave-Butters-Kelley Indexes, Monthly GDP Growth, Cycle component, %
rics.meaning: Brave-Butters-Kelley Indexes, Monthly GDP Growth, cyclical component — the cyclical-fluctuation portion of the BBK monthly GDP estimate (factor model).
rics.how_to_use: Decomposes BBK GDP into trend + cyclical + irregular. The cyclical component is the meaningful business-cycle signal — strips out trend growth and noise. Negative readings precede recessions; positive readings = expansion phase.

rics.description: Brave-Butters-Kelley Indexes, Monthly GDP Growth, Cycle component, Lagging, %
rics.meaning: BBK Indexes, Monthly GDP Growth, cyclical-trend component — the trend portion of the cyclical decomposition. Underlying potential-growth pace.
rics.how_to_use: Smoother than the cyclical component. Tracks 'trend' GDP growth — currently ~1.8-2.0% reflecting demographic + productivity drivers. Sustained drops below 1.5% suggest secular-stagnation concerns.

rics.description: Brave-Butters-Kelley Indexes, Monthly GDP Growth, Cycle component, Leading, %
rics.meaning: BBK Indexes, Monthly GDP Growth, cyclical-cycle component — the pure business-cycle deviation from trend. Negative = below-trend, positive = above-trend.
rics.how_to_use: Useful for output-gap estimation. Sustained negative readings = recession-territory output gap. Pair with CBO output gap estimates for triangulated read.

rics.description: Brave-Butters-Kelley Indexes, Monthly GDP Growth, Irregular component, %
rics.meaning: BBK Indexes, Monthly GDP Growth, irregular component — the residual noise in the BBK decomposition. Captures one-off shocks not explained by trend or cycle.
rics.how_to_use: Spikes during major shocks (2020 COVID, 2008 financial crisis). Used to remove temporary distortions before reading the cyclical signal. Markets typically ignore the irregular component — focus on cyclical.

rics.description: Brave-Butters-Kelley Indexes, Monthly GDP Growth, Trend component, %
rics.meaning: BBK GDP growth, trend component.
rics.how_to_use: Slow-moving trend. Useful for productivity/labor-supply growth read.

rics.description: Chicago Fed CFMMI, National Activity Index
rics.meaning: Chicago Fed National Activity Index (CFNAI) — weighted average of 85 monthly indicators (production, employment, sales, consumption). Composite real-time activity gauge.
rics.how_to_use: Above 0 = above trend; sustained -0.7 (3-mo avg) signals recession. Most-watched composite activity indicator alongside Conference Board LEI. Released monthly on a 1-month lag.

rics.description: Chicago Fed National Activity Index - Actual, Index, USD
rics.meaning: Chicago Fed National Activity Index — alternative release of the same CFNAI data. Captures real-time activity from 85 monthly indicators.
rics.how_to_use: Cross-check against aUSCFNA. Both are the same CFNAI but at different release vintages. Above-zero = above-trend growth; sustained -0.7 (3-mo MA) signals recession.

rics.description: New York Fed, Weekly Economic Index
rics.meaning: NY Fed Weekly Economic Index — weekly real GDP-equivalent growth rate. Highest-frequency real-economy gauge.
rics.how_to_use: Updated every Tuesday based on 10 weekly indicators. Translates to a quarterly GDP nowcast equivalent. Useful for tracking the cycle between BEA quarterly releases.

rics.description: Kansas Fed, Financial Stress Index
rics.meaning: Kansas City Fed Financial Stress Index.
rics.how_to_use: Composite financial-conditions gauge. Spikes during 2008, March 2020, March 2023 (regional bank stress).

rics.description: Labour Market n.i.e, Kansas City Fed Labor Market Conditions Indicator, Level of Activity
rics.meaning: Kansas City Fed Labor Market Conditions Index — composite of 24 labor-market indicators (claims, NFP, hours, wages, JOLTS, household survey). Available in level and momentum forms.
rics.how_to_use: Higher-frequency labor-market gauge than the BLS monthly print alone. Sustained negative readings precede labor-market deterioration. Pair with Sahm Rule (aUSRSAHMN/A) and CB ETI (aUSEMPTR) for triangulated cycle call.

rics.description: Labour Market n.i.e, Kansas City Fed Labor Market Conditions Indicator, Momentum
rics.meaning: KC Fed Labor Market Conditions Index — momentum component (vs level component aUSKCLMCAR). Captures rate-of-change in labor-market conditions.
rics.how_to_use: Leading indicator: momentum turns before levels. Negative momentum + positive level = labor market is good but cooling. Watch for sustained negative-momentum readings as recession-leading signal.

rics.description: Federal Reserve Bank of St. Louis, St. Louis Financial Stress Index
rics.meaning: St. Louis Fed Financial Stress Index — composite of 18 weekly financial-market indicators (yields, spreads, vol). Z-score format; zero = normal stress.
rics.how_to_use: Real-time financial-conditions gauge. Spikes during crises (2008 ~6, 2020 ~5, 2023 SVB ~1). Sustained readings >2 indicate market stress beyond normal volatility — Fed often acts when sustained.

rics.description: Federal Reserve Bank of St. Louis, St. Louis Financial Stress Index
rics.meaning: St. Louis Financial Stress Index — alternative release. Same conceptual measure as aUSSFSIR.
rics.how_to_use: Cross-check series. Use whichever has fresher data. Useful for confirming stress regimes — both must agree for confident signal.

rics.description: Federal Reserve Bank of St. Louis, St. Louis Financial Stress Index
rics.meaning: St. Louis Fed FSI — daily.
rics.how_to_use: Highest-frequency stress read.

rics.description: NCREIF: TIMBERLAND INDEX RETURNS
rics.meaning: NCREIF Timberland Index returns.
rics.how_to_use: Niche real-asset class. Low correlation to stocks/bonds; institutional allocator interest.

rics.description: Standard & Poors, 500 Composite, Cyclically Adjusted Price Earnings Ratio P/E10 or CAPE (Shiller)
rics.meaning: S&P 500 Cyclically Adjusted P/E (Shiller CAPE / P/E10).
rics.how_to_use: Long-run valuation gauge: price / 10-yr inflation-adjusted earnings. >30 historically signals lower forward returns.

rics.description: Standard & Poors, 500 Composite, Index, 12 Month As Reported Earnings per Share (top down)
rics.meaning: S&P 500 12-month trailing as-reported EPS (top-down).
rics.how_to_use: Earnings denominator for P/E. Compare against operating EPS for accounting-quality drift.

rics.description: Standard & Poors, 500 Composite, Index, 12 Month Cash Dividends per Share (top down)
rics.meaning: S&P 500 trailing 12-month dividends per share (index basis) — total cash dividends paid by S&P 500 constituents over the last four quarters, scaled to the index. Updated continuously by S&P Dow Jones Indices.
rics.how_to_use: Smoother and more cyclical than EPS — companies cut dividends only in extreme stress. Pair with the dividend yield (aUSSPDIVY) for a valuation cross-check, and with EPS to compute the payout ratio. Slow-moving baseline for total-return decomposition.

rics.description: Standard & Poors, 500 Composite, Index, Dividend Yield
rics.meaning: S&P 500 dividend yield — index dividends / price.
rics.how_to_use: Low yields (sub-2%) reflect post-2010 buyback preference. Compare to 10Y Treasury for equity risk premium.

rics.description: Standard & Poors, 500 Composite, Index
rics.meaning: S&P 500 Composite Index level.
rics.how_to_use: Headline US equity benchmark. Cap-weighted; ~7 megacaps drive much of recent return.

rics.description: Coincident Index
rics.meaning: Conference Board Coincident Economic Index — current-state composite (employment, income, output, sales).
rics.how_to_use: Tracks GDP contemporaneously. Use the LEI/CEI ratio: when LEI growth is below CEI growth for an extended period, recession risk rises.

rics.description: Commercial and industrial loans outstanding
rics.meaning: Commercial and industrial loans outstanding.
rics.how_to_use: Business-lending cycle gauge. Slows ahead of recessions; SLOOS tightening leads by 1-2 quarters.

rics.description: Index of stock prices, 500 common stocks
rics.meaning: Index of stock prices, 500 common stocks — embedded in BCI.
rics.how_to_use: Component of leading economic indicators.

rics.description: Labour Market n.i.e, Employment Trends - Acutal
rics.meaning: Employment Trends Index — Conference Board, actual.
rics.how_to_use: Labor-market composite. Companion to NFP/UR.

rics.description: Labour Market n.i.e, The Conference Board Employment Trends Index (ETI)
rics.meaning: Conference Board Employment Trends Index (ETI) — composite of eight labor-market indicators (claims, NFIB hiring plans, jobs hard-to-get, temp employment, hours, ratio of involuntary part-timers, JOLTS hires, employment in manufacturing). Released monthly.
rics.how_to_use: Leads NFP turning points by 2-3 months — historically an excellent labor-market inflection caller. Sustained declines flag rising recession risk before payrolls weaken. Pair with the Sahm Rule for a triangulated read.

rics.description: Lagging Index
rics.meaning: Conference Board Lagging Economic Index — confirmatory, not predictive. Inflation, ULC, prime rate, ratio of consumer credit to income.
rics.how_to_use: Use to confirm cycle turns AFTER the fact. CEI/LAG ratio is itself a leading indicator: lagging components reflect built-up imbalances.

rics.description: Leading Credit Index
rics.meaning: Leading Credit Index — component of LEI.
rics.how_to_use: Credit-spread-based forward signal.

rics.description: Leading Index
rics.meaning: Conference Board Leading Economic Index (LEI) — composite of 10 leading indicators (yield curve, claims, permits, S&P 500, ISM new orders, etc.).
rics.how_to_use: Sustained 6-month declines historically signal recession with 6-12 month lead. False-positive in 2022-23 (predicted recession that didn't materialize as Fed soft-landed). Use alongside yield curve, not in isolation.

rics.description: Leading Index, Interest rate spread, 10-year Treasury bonds less federal funds
rics.meaning: 10Y Treasury minus fed funds rate — recession-warning yield-curve spread.
rics.how_to_use: Inverted curve (negative spread) has preceded every US recession since 1970. Watch slope dynamics, not just sign.

rics.description: Leading Index, Stock prices, 500 common stocks
rics.meaning: Stock prices, 500 common stocks — LEI component.
rics.how_to_use: Embedded equity proxy in LEI.

rics.description: Leading index chg- Actual, Chg P/P
rics.meaning: Leading index change MoM, actual.
rics.how_to_use: Most market-moving LEI series at release. -0.3% MoM consensus is the threshold for hawk/dove read.

rics.description: United Kingdom, stock prices
rics.meaning: UK stock prices — included for cross-country reference.
rics.how_to_use: Niche; reference series.
